hypothesis: FP16-accumulate Q.K^T in the prefill kernel _attn_fwd (both the unmasked causal loop and the masked loop): load q once, pre-scale it by qk_scale = scale*log2(e) in fp32 and cast to fp16; cast each K tile to fp16 and compute qk = tl.dot(q16, k.to(fp16), out_dtype=fp16).to(fp32), which is already in the log2 domain, so the softmax becomes m_new = max(m_i, rowmax(qk)), p = exp2(qk - m_new). P.V stays fp16-acc (exp 12); m_i, l_i and the running acc stay fp32. Decode/split kernels unchanged.
rationale: Exp 12 moved P.V to the 2x-rate fp16-accumulate mma.sync and won (1.150 -> 1.185). Q.K^T is now the only fp32-accumulate mma and half the prefill FLOPs: prefill_32768 at 37.7 ms is ~233 TFLOPS, ~84% of the mixed ceiling (QK at 209.5 + PV at 419 TFLOPS -> ~31.5 ms). Making QK fp16-acc lowers that ceiling to ~21 ms. Exp 12's notes listed this as the follow-up. Precision: fp16 has 3 more mantissa bits than bf16, so q/k casts are exact or finer; the k=128 accumulation in fp16 gives ~1e-3 relative error on logits of magnitude <= ~7 (after pre-scaling), i.e. a few 1e-3 in p, expected to keep max_row_rel well under the ~0.009 tolerance (currently ~0.0023). Pre-scaling q by 0.1275 before the cast gives ~8x more overflow headroom than fp16-casting raw q and also drops the per-element scale multiply in the unmasked loop.
expected_effect: Prefill rows 5-15% faster (largest on prefill_16384/32768, where the kernel is mma-bound), decode unchanged; geomean ~+3-6%. Risk: correctness margin shrinks; if check shows rel error near tolerance, abandon.
